correctness.rationale: Independently, the original-vertex block of exp(-it A_S) is cos(t sqrt(B B^T)) by the power series, with B the unsigned incidence matrix. The constant zero-mode contribution has time-averaged square F_0(u,u)^2; distinct positive frequencies have vanishing cross terms and each cosine has mean square 1/2. The equation B^T f=0 forces opposite values on endpoints, so in a connected bipartite graph F_0(u,u)=1/n and otherwise it is zero. This also covers n=2 and nonregular graphs. On S(K_n), the positive squared frequencies 2(n-1) and n-2 have multiplicities 1 and n-1. Each signed eigenspace projects half its trace onto each bipartition, by the singular-vector pairing, and symmetry is transitive on each part. With part size k the weights per sign are 1/(2k) and (n-1)/(2k), and the remaining weight is 1-n/k. Taking k=n or k=n(n-1)/2 and summing squared weights recovers both fractions and their difference. The zero weight vanishes at n=3. The cubic factor is negative at 4 and 5, positive at 6, and increasing thereafter, giving the full cutoff and limits.
residual_risks: The bounded exact replay corroborates the clique calculation only; the analytic argument is required for all orders and all connected graphs.

value.rationale: The adjacency return invariant tests whether a once-subdivision transfers long-time return from hubs to newly inserted low-degree vertices. The exact clique cutoff answers this for all orders, and the edge-kernel term identifies the mechanism behind a limiting gap of 1/2 rather than just exhibiting a few examples. The pointwise identity also isolates exactly when bipartiteness prevents exact halving.
residual_risks: No localization claim beyond vertex return in the specified adjacency model; only the original-vertex identity is general in G.
